title: Atlas refused candidate record
description: A relation the Atlas considered and refused: what was read, which rule refused it and why. It is the Atlas's design ruling, never a fact about the world and never an edge. Being in data/refused_candidates.json is the ruling: there is no status field (RR-6). Status: accepted (S13 opening review, 2026-10-02; D-109). This file is the one home of the record shape and of the reason vocabulary's definitions. The rule that refuses candidates is edge-dataset.md §1 (D-089). Shared shapes (relation types, entity endpoints, claim and source IDs, the Verifier's read) are referenced, never copied.

id.description: cand- plus three digits, assigned in the order of edge-dataset.md §1's rows at the migration (S12), then in order of creation; never reused. A rule-made ID like RI-1 is not possible: an endpoint may have no record, and a row may name two parties (D-109).

relation_types.description: The relation type or types the candidate would have had.

source_entities.description: The subject or subjects of the sentence '<source> <type> <target>' the candidate would have stated.

target_entities.description: The object or objects of that sentence.

item.description: supplies only: the item named, as the row names it. Left out when none is named.

considered.description: What was read: a claim, or a sentence that is not a claim. Never evidence for anything (D-109).

reasons.description: Why it is not an edge, as codes. The Extractor codes them from the reasoning; the human reviews them.

reasoning.description: The Atlas's explanation (INTERPRETATION), verbatim from the edge-dataset.md §1 row it was migrated from.

ruling.description: The decision in decisions.md that refused the candidate.

endpoint.description: An entity record's ID, or an explicit state for a party or item with no record. Never a placeholder ID (RR-7, V-9).

no_record.description: A party or item the Atlas has no record for. The name is as the candidate row wrote it; it identifies nothing and asserts nothing. A check fails if it is the name or an alias of an existing record (RC-4).

considered_sentence.description: A sentence that is not a claim: its source, where it is, the quoted words (left out when the row quotes none) and whether the Verifier re-read it.

anchor.description: As the row quoted it; an ellipsis marks words the row left out.

read.description: The Verifier's re-read, as on a claim's citation, or an explicit state.

state_not_recorded.description: The row gave no locator, and none has been recorded since.

state_not_re_read.description: The Verifier has not re-read this sentence in the registered bytes. The quote is the Atlas's record of what was considered, not checked evidence.

oneOf.description: The sentence does not state this relation itself: it names the parties together, says what a thing is for, or states possession, production or group membership, which the type's evidence expectation does not accept (RR-1, ER-2).
The sentence states a relation of another type.
The sentence is about a company in general, not the product or item the edge would name (ER-9).
A party has no record, and this evidence cannot create one.
The item has no record, and the Atlas does not stretch it to one that exists (ER-9).
The relation type is time-sensitive and the evidence is older than the freshness horizon (F-1).
